The quiet collapse of the reinsurance market

Three quarters of losses, one regulator asleep, and a market that has repriced without telling anyone who buys from it.

The first sign was a footnote. In the fourth-quarter filing of a mid-sized Bermudian reinsurer, the reserve development line moved by a number large enough that three analysts asked about it on the call, and the answer given was not an answer.
